title: Throughput contracting and adaptive autoscale protocol for Dedicated capacity
creator: Aisha Romero
description: Create a repeatable provisioning and approval protocol that contracts throughput commitments, binds autoscaling policy templates, and sets fleet-level controls for Dedicated capacity. The deliverable is a product playbook + flow automations in Console that operators and sales can use to intake reservation requests, validate SLA targets, and produce a binding capacity agreement with clear rollback/fallback behavior.
background: Customers frequently request committed throughput with cost predictability and guarantees. Current reservation flows collect rudimentary inputs but lack a defensible decisioning layer for throughput SLAs, autoscaling guardrails, and fleet-level budget caps. This leads to overprovisioning, unexpected degradation, or manual back-and-forth between Sales, Solutions, and Infra.
scope: Design intake forms, approval decision matrix, autoscale policy templates (min/max, burst windows, cooling periods), and a 'contract' artifact that ties requested throughput to an enforced autoscale profile and fleet control knobs. Implement Console UI changes to surface the contract and hooks for operators to approve or request changes. Hook the decision outputs to Reserved provisioning automation (backend work lives in ENG).
out_of_scope: Billing invoice generation, long-term usage reconciliations, private deployment on-prem installer changes (those will be separate PMs). Deep kernel/runtime optimizations for throughput beyond templated recommendations.
goals: Reduce time-to-approve for dedicated reservation requests from days to under 8 business hours for standard profiles
Ensure committed-throughput requests are paired with autoscale profiles that limit downside risk to other customers on shared fleet
Automate production of a machine-readable 'capacity contract' that can be enforced by provisioning systems
Provide operators with a clear escalation path and rollback options when commitments cannot be met
success_metrics: Median approval time for standard reservation requests <= 8 hours
< 5% of reservations require manual capacity rebalancing after provisioning
Customer satisfaction (NPS) for onboarding flow >= 8/10 in pilot cohort
Automated contract generation coverage >= 90% of inbound reservation requests
acceptance_criteria: Intake form captures required throughput SLA, expected QPS, workload distribution, peak sequence length, and preferred region
Decision matrix maps request to one of: standard-approved, require-ops-review, require-capacity-sourcing
Console shows generated contract with autoscale profile linked, and operators can approve/reject with a single click
Provisioning automation consumes contract artifact and returns provisioning status to Console
Operator runbook published and accessible from Console (approval steps, common remediation patterns, escalation contacts)
implementation_plan: Sprint 1: Finalize intake form fields and decision matrix with Solutions and Sales input
Sprint 2: Define autoscale policy templates (min/max tokens/sec, burst windows, cooldown) with Eng and Reliability
Sprint 3: Build Console UI for contract preview and operator approvals (mockups -> prototype)
Sprint 4: Wire contract artifact to provisioning automation and test happy path in staging
Sprint 5: Pilot with two enterprise customers, collect feedback, iterate
rollout_plan: Internal alpha: ops + sales use for non-critical reservations (2 weeks)
Controlled pilot: 2 paying customers, monitor SLOs and rebalancing (4 weeks)
General availability: open to all accounts with telemetry and opt-in enforcement (target release dedicated-2026.04)
risks: Underestimating real workload variance causes SLO breaches despite contracts
Autoscale templates too permissive lead to noisy neighbor impact
Operators bypass the flow and create ad-hoc reservations reducing automation value
Provisioning automation fails in edge cases causing partial allocations
mitigations: Require workload telemetry (past 14 days) as part of intake to calibrate templates
Constrain template burst windows and implement automatic cool-down enforcement
Add audit logging and approval gating to discourage bypass; track bypass rate as metric
Create a staged provisioning test harness and rollback semantics; add canary allocations
open_questions: What margin (percent headroom) should be required between requested throughput and template max to reduce breach risk?
Should we support contractual fallbacks to lower-tier models automatically if capacity is constrained?
How will commercial/legal teams want the generated 'contract' to be surfaced — PDF, signed doc, or machine-readable append to customer account?
What SLA credits or remediation policy do we promise if autoscale/contract fails?
